abstract:
Let $m\ge 3$ be odd and let $S=\mathbf{P}^1_\lambda\setminus\{0,\infty,1,-1\}\subset\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$ be the one-dimensional symmetric slice parametrizing degree-$m$ cyclic covers $C_\lambda	o\mathbf{P}^1$ branched at $(-1,-\lambda,0,\lambda,1,\infty)$ with a $(2,2,1,1)$-symmetric branch weight tuple $\mathbf{a}$ under an involution $h\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ ($H=\{1,h\}$). Unlike on $\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$, under the local non-resonance conditions of Lemma 2.1 (satisfied by all $t\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ on our CRT families), every puncture of $S$ is a simultaneous multi-point collision whose local monodromy generator $g_p(t)$ ($p\in\{1,-1,0,\infty\}$) on $V_t=H_1(C_\lambda,\mathbf{C})_t$ and non-scalar powers $g_p(t)^k
otin\mathbf{C}^	imes I_4$ satisfy $\operatorname{rank}(g_p(t)-cI_4)\ge 2$ and $\operatorname{rank}(g_p(t)^k-cI_4)\ge 2$ for all $c\in\mathbf{C}^	imes$, so no local puncture generator or non-scalar power is a rank-$1$ pseudoreflection or transvection; moreover, for composite $m=a\cdot m'$ ($\gcd(a,m')=1$) the CRT multiplier $v\equiv(-1,+1)\pmod{(a,m')}
otin\pm H$ shares identical projective puncture spectra with $t=1$ and collides on $g_1g_0$ and $g_1g_{-1}$.

We establish an unconditional global braid-monodromy rigidity and cyclotomic separation theory on $S$: (1) cyclotomic linear disjointness in the $g_1(t)$-eigenbasis proves the adjoint dichotomy $\mathfrak{g}\in\{\{0\},\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbf{C})\}$ (Theorem A); (2) for every $m=15N$ with $\gcd(N,30)=1$, Chebyshev–Laurent and Ramanujan-sum trace averages of $(g_1g_0)^2$ prove factorwise Zariski density in $\operatorname{SU}(J(t))\simeq\operatorname{SU}(d_t-1,5-d_t)$ up to $\mu_{15N}$ scalars, while expanding $	au_t(g_1^2g_0)$ in the dual basis $\mathcal{B}_{15}$ over $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_N)$ separates all non-trivial cosets $[t]
eq[\pm 1]$ (Theorem B); (3) $g_1^2g_0$ uniformly separates $v\equiv(-1,+1)\pmod{(a,m')}$ from $\pm H$ for coprime odd $a,m'\ge 3$ (Theorem C); and (4) four Galois involution projectors on $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_a)\otimes\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_b)\otimes\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_N)$ extend density and length-$3$ separation to the three-factor family $m=a\cdot b\cdot N$ ($\gcd(N,30)=1$), alongside four method-boundary examples (Theorem D). By Goursat's lemma, this determines the generic derived Mumford–Tate group $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})_{\mathrm{der}}=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(J(t))$ and endomorphism algebra $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_m)^H$ over $S$, and on characterwise $(2,2)$-balanced subfamilies ($d_t=3$) gives $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(2,2)$, reducing all-powers Hodge algebraicity to the separate determinant-cycle input on individual factors (Corollary E).

change_summary: Revision v3 of hodge_conjecture_114 incorporating all four local wording and notation improvements from the v2 review: (1) In the paragraph following Eq. (1.9a), identified the factorwise Galois automorphism sigma_{e_a}^{-1} x sigma_{e_b}^{-1} x sigma_{e_N}^{-1} with sigma_{t_ref} (since t_ref = e_q^{-1} mod q) and described the CRT residue map on unit groups (Z/mZ)^x -> (Z/aZ)^x x (Z/bZ)^x x (Z/NZ)^x as the multiplicative group isomorphism induced by the CRT ring isomorphism on Z/mZ; (2) Replaced the shorthand 'g_p(t)^k != I_4' with the exact non-scalar condition 'g_p(t)^k notin C^x I_4' across the Abstract, Section 1.1, Theorem A(1), Lemma 2.1, and Section 8.3; (3) In the opening paragraph of Section 7.3 and Table 9.2, distinguished the companion-template examples (b.1) at (9, 5, 7) and (b.2) at (3, 7, 11) from the generalized primary family (1.9) of Theorems 7.1-7.2 (which directly contains (b.3) at (5, 3, 7)), while (b.4) at (5, 7, 3) lies outside gcd(N, 30) = 1; (4) In Section 7.1 Case 3a, restricted the monotonicity statement f'(X) >= 103/25 > 0 to [-2, -9/5] (where X_3 in (-2, -9/5) is isolated), and shortened the second paragraph of the abstract.
title: Braid Monodromy Rigidity on One-Dimensional Symmetric Cyclic Prym Slices: Adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_4$-Dichotomy, Ramanujan-Sum Trace Averages, and Length-Three Cyclotomic Separation
